blurb.en: Three different answers to 'what is a typical value?': the statistics module's mean, median, mode and multimode, and a median written by hand - sort, then take the middle, or the average of the middle two.
blurb.zh: 「典型的值是多少」有三种不同的回答：statistics 模块的 mean、median、mode 与 multimode，再手写一个中位数——先排序，再取正中间那个，或中间两个的平均。

en: The mean adds everything up and divides by how many there are; the median is the middle value once the list is sorted; the mode is the value that turns up most often. For the marks 7, 3, 9, 3, 5, 8, 3 they are three different numbers: the mean is 5.43 (to 2 places), the median is 5 and the mode is 3.

The hand-written median sorts a new list (the caller's list is left alone) and uses mid = n // 2. With an odd count there is one middle value, at index mid. With an even count there are two, at mid - 1 and mid, and the median is their average - for 4, 1, 6, 2 that is the average of 2 and 4, which is 3.0. The function always returns a float so that both cases give the same type; statistics.median returns the middle value itself when the count is odd, so it prints 5 where this function prints 5.0.

statistics.mode gives one answer even when there is a tie: for the shoe sizes 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9 both 6 and 8 appear twice, and mode returns 6, the one it met first. statistics.multimode returns every tied value, here [6, 8]. The mode is also the only one of the three averages that works on words: the favourite colour in the demo is red.

Why have three? One huge value drags the mean but hardly moves the median. For the pay list 21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 250 the mean is 61.5 - more than anyone except one person earns - while the median is 24.5, which describes the typical person much better.

The page's checker compares median with a version that never sorts: for each value it counts how many values are smaller and how many are not larger, and picks the one in the right position. It runs on hundreds of made-up lists, odd and even lengths alike, many with the two middle values different - the case that catches 'always take one middle value'.
zh: 平均数把所有数加起来再除以个数；中位数是排好序后正中间的那个；众数是出现次数最多的那个。对成绩 7, 3, 9, 3, 5, 8, 3 来说，它们是三个不同的数：平均数 5.43（保留 2 位），中位数 5，众数 3。

手写的中位数先排出一个新列表（调用者的列表不动），再取 mid = n // 2。个数是奇数时正中间只有一个数，下标就是 mid；个数是偶数时正中间有两个，下标是 mid - 1 与 mid，中位数是它们的平均——对 4, 1, 6, 2 来说就是 2 与 4 的平均，3.0。这个函数总是返回小数，让两种情况类型一致；statistics.median 在奇数个时直接返回那个数本身，所以它打印 5，而这个函数打印 5.0。
有并列时 statistics.mode 也只给一个答案：鞋码 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9 里 6 和 8 都出现两次，mode 返回先遇到的 6。statistics.multimode 把并列的都返回，这里是 [6, 8]。三种平均里只有众数能用在文字上：演示里最受欢迎的颜色是 red。
为什么要三种？一个特别大的值会把平均数拽走，却几乎不动中位数。工资 21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 250 的平均数是 61.5——除了一个人，谁都没挣这么多——而中位数是 24.5，更能代表一个典型的人。
页面的检查器拿一个从不排序的版本和 median 对答案：对每个值数一数有几个比它小、几个不比它大，挑出排在正确位置上的那个。它在几百个随手造的列表上跑，奇数长和偶数长都有，而且很多列表中间两个数不相等——这正是能抓住「偶数个也只取一个中间数」的情形。

lineNotes.en: Integer division: for 7 values mid is 3 (the fourth value, the true middle); for 4 values it is 2, the right-hand one of the middle pair.
lineNotes.zh: 整除：7 个数时 mid 是 3（第四个，正中间）；4 个数时是 2，指向中间那一对里靠右的那个。

lineNotes.en: float makes the odd case return a decimal too, so the function's result has one type whatever the length.
lineNotes.zh: float 让奇数个的情形也返回小数：不论长度，函数结果都是同一种类型。

lineNotes.en: multimode returns a list of every value that shares the top count, in the order they first appear.
lineNotes.zh: multimode 返回一个列表，装着所有并列最多的值，按第一次出现的顺序。

marks: [7, 3, 9, 3, 5, 8, 3]
sorted: [3, 3, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9]
mean: 5.43
median: 5 5.0
mode: 3
even count: [1, 2, 4, 6]
median: 3.0 3.0
shoe sizes: [5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9]
multimode: [6, 8]
mode: 6
favourite colour: red
pay: [21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 250]
mean: 61.5
median: 24.5

title.zh: 总体标准差与样本标准差

blurb.en: The standard deviation divided by n or by n - 1: ddof=0 and ddof=1 in NumPy, pstdev and stdev in the statistics module. Then z-scores, and the values more than two standard deviations from the mean.
blurb.zh: 标准差除以 n 还是除以 n - 1：NumPy 里的 ddof=0 与 ddof=1，statistics 模块里的 pstdev 与 stdev。再算 z 分数，找出离均值超过两个标准差的值。

en: The standard deviation measures how far values typically sit from their mean: square each distance from the mean, average the squares, take the square root. The question is what 'average' divides by. If the list is the whole population, divide by n. If it is a sample taken from a bigger population and you want to estimate the population's spread, divide by n - 1.

Why n - 1? A sample's values are always a little closer to their own mean than to the true mean of the population - the sample mean was worked out from those very values, so it sits in the middle of them. The squared distances therefore come out slightly too small, and dividing by one less makes up for it. With only two values the difference is large: for 4 and 8 the population version gives 2.0 and the sample version 2.828.

NumPy's std takes a keyword ddof, short for delta degrees of freedom: it divides by n - ddof. The default is ddof=0, the population version; ddof=1 gives the sample version. The statistics module has one function for each: pstdev (population) and stdev (sample). For the ten lap times in the demo, whose mean is 12.3, the population standard deviation is 0.794 and the sample one 0.837 - and the statistics module gives the same two numbers.

A z-score says how many standard deviations a value is from the mean: (value - mean) / standard deviation. The demo works out all ten at once on the array, and prints them five to a line. A common rule of thumb calls a value an outlier when its z-score is more than 2 or less than -2. Here only the lap of 14.6 seconds qualifies, with a z-score of 2.9; every other lap is within one standard deviation of the mean.

sample_sd converts NumPy's answer with float before rounding it, so it returns an ordinary Python number. The page's checker compares it with a pure-Python version that uses exact whole-number arithmetic - n times the sum of squares minus the square of the sum - and only takes the square root at the end.
zh: 标准差量的是各个值通常离均值多远：每个值到均值的距离平方，把这些平方求平均，再开方。问题在于这个「平均」除以什么。如果列表就是整个总体，除以 n；如果它只是从更大的总体里抽出来的样本、而你想估计总体的离散程度，就除以 n - 1。
为什么是 n - 1？样本的值离它们自己的均值，总比离总体真正的均值近一点——样本均值就是用这些值算出来的，天然坐在它们中间。所以平方距离算出来偏小，少除一个正好补回来。只有两个值时差别很大：4 和 8，总体的写法得 2.0，样本的写法得 2.828。

NumPy 的 std 有个关键字参数 ddof（delta degrees of freedom，自由度的修正量）：它除以 n - ddof。默认 ddof=0，是总体的写法；ddof=1 是样本的写法。statistics 模块里各有一个函数：pstdev（总体）与 stdev（样本）。演示里十个单圈时间的均值是 12.3，总体标准差 0.794，样本标准差 0.837——statistics 模块给出的也是这两个数。
z 分数说的是一个值离均值有几个标准差：(值 - 均值) / 标准差。演示在数组上一次算出全部十个，每行打印五个。常用的经验规则：z 分数大于 2 或小于 -2 的值算离群值。这里只有 14.6 秒那一圈够格，z 分数是 2.9；其余每一圈离均值都不到一个标准差。
sample_sd 先用 float 转换 NumPy 的答案再舍入，所以返回的是普通的 Python 数。页面的检查器拿一个纯 Python 版本和它对答案：用整数精确地算「n 乘平方和，减去和的平方」，最后一步才开方。

lineNotes.en: dtype=float makes the array hold decimals even when every value in xs is a whole number.
lineNotes.zh: dtype=float 让数组装的是小数，哪怕 xs 里全是整数。

lineNotes.en: ddof=0 is the default, written out here so the two versions can be compared side by side.
lineNotes.zh: ddof=0 本来就是默认值，这里写出来，好跟样本的写法并排对照。

lineNotes.en: tolist turns the NumPy array into a plain list of Python floats before printing.
lineNotes.zh: tolist 在打印前把 NumPy 数组变成装着 Python 小数的普通列表。

population sd (ddof=0): 0.794
sample sd (ddof=1): 0.837
pstdev: 0.794
stdev: 0.837
two values, ddof=0: 2.0
two values, ddof=1: 2.828
z-scores:
[-0.25 -0.63  0.13 -0.38 -0.5 ]
[-0.13  2.9   0.   -0.76 -0.38]

title.zh: 照定义算皮尔逊相关系数

blurb.en: The correlation coefficient built step by step with NumPy arrays: deviations from the mean, the sum of their products, divided by the square root of the product of the two sums of squares. Then what r does and does not tell you.
blurb.zh: 用 NumPy 数组一步步算出相关系数：离均值的偏差、偏差乘积之和，再除以两个平方和之积的平方根。然后看 r 说明了什么、没说明什么。

en: Pearson's r measures how close a set of points (x, y) comes to lying on a straight line. First take every x away from the mean of x, and every y away from the mean of y: these are the deviations dx and dy. Multiply them item by item and add up: a point above average in both, or below average in both, adds a positive amount; a point above in one and below in the other adds a negative amount. Finally divide by the square root of (sum of dx squared) times (sum of dy squared), which scales the answer to lie between -1 and 1.
Everything is done on whole arrays at once - x - x.mean() takes the mean away from every item in one step - which is the vectorised style from the NumPy Basics page.

What the numbers mean: r = 1 is a perfect rising straight line, r = -1 a perfect falling one, and r near 0 means no straight-line relationship. In the demo, hours of revision against marks gives 0.964, a strong positive correlation. A list made exactly from 2 times hours plus 1 gives 1.0 and one made from 100 minus 5 times hours gives -1.0, whatever the gradient. Hours against shoe size gives -0.124: nothing to speak of.

The U-shaped curve is the warning: its y values are (hours - 4.5) squared, completely determined by x, yet r is 0.0. The rising half and the falling half cancel out. r only measures straight-line relationships; a strong curved one can hide behind r = 0.

The last lines print the deviations themselves, from -3.5 to 3.5 in steps of 1, and show that they add up to 0.0 - deviations from the mean always do, which is why the formula multiplies or squares them instead of just adding them.

Compare this with Pearson's r from NumPy's Matrix, which gets the same number from a single library call. The page's checker compares both with a pure-Python version that uses exact whole-number sums and never works out a deviation.
zh: 皮尔逊 r 量的是一组点 (x, y) 离「排成一条直线」有多近。先让每个 x 减去 x 的均值、每个 y 减去 y 的均值：这就是偏差 dx 与 dy。逐项相乘再相加：两个都高于均值、或两个都低于均值的点贡献正数；一个高一个低的点贡献负数。最后除以（dx 平方和）乘（dy 平方和）的平方根，把结果缩放到 -1 与 1 之间。
所有计算都在整个数组上一次完成——x - x.mean() 一步就让每一项都减去均值——这是「NumPy 基础」一页讲过的向量化写法。
数字的含义：r = 1 是一条完美上升的直线，r = -1 是完美下降的直线，r 接近 0 说明没有直线关系。演示里复习小时数对成绩得 0.964，强正相关。用 2 乘小时数加 1 精确造出的列表得 1.0，用 100 减 5 乘小时数造出的得 -1.0——与斜率大小无关。小时数对鞋码得 -0.124：谈不上相关。
U 形曲线是个警告：它的 y 值是 (小时数 - 4.5) 的平方，完全由 x 决定，r 却是 0.0。上升的一半与下降的一半正好抵消。r 只量直线关系；很强的曲线关系可能躲在 r = 0 后面。
最后几行把偏差本身打印出来：从 -3.5 到 3.5，每步 1，并且它们加起来是 0.0——离均值的偏差加起来总是 0，所以公式要把它们相乘或平方，而不是直接相加。
对照「用 NumPy 的相关矩阵求 r」，它一次库函数调用就得到同一个数。页面的检查器拿一个纯 Python 版本和这两个都对答案：它用整数精确求和，从头到尾不算一个偏差。

lineNotes.en: One subtraction for the whole array: the mean of y is taken away from every item.
lineNotes.zh: 整个数组一次减法：每一项都减去 y 的均值。

lineNotes.en: The deviations from the mean always add up to zero.
lineNotes.zh: 离均值的偏差加起来总是零。

run.expect:
hours vs marks: 0.964
exact straight line: 1.0
exact falling line: -1.0
hours vs shoe size: -0.124
a U-shaped curve: 0.0
deviations from the mean:
[-3.5 -2.5 -1.5 -0.5  0.5  1.5  2.5  3.5]
they add up to: 0.0

title.zh: 用 NumPy 的相关矩阵求 r

blurb.en: The same coefficient from one call: np.corrcoef returns a whole correlation matrix, and r is the entry in row 0, column 1. Then three variables at once, and why a strong correlation is not a cause.
blurb.zh: 同一个系数，一次调用：np.corrcoef 返回一整个相关矩阵，r 是第 0 行第 1 列那一格。再一次看三个变量，以及为什么强相关不等于因果。

en: Given two lists, np.corrcoef does not return one number. It treats them as two variables and returns a 2 x 2 matrix: row i, column j holds r between variable i and variable j. The diagonal compares each variable with itself, so it is always 1; the two off-diagonal entries are the same r, because the correlation of x with y is the correlation of y with x. That is why pearson picks out row 0, column 1 - it is the only number in the matrix you did not already know.

For hours of revision against marks the matrix has 1 on the diagonal and 0.964 in the other two places, the same r as Pearson's r from Its Definition. Swapping the order of the arguments gives 0.964 again.

Give np.corrcoef a list of several lists and every one is a variable: the demo passes temperature, ice creams sold and sunburn cases and gets a 3 x 3 matrix. Temperature against ice creams is 0.997, temperature against sunburns 0.994, and ice creams against sunburns 0.992.

That last number is a strong correlation, yet eating ice cream does not give anyone sunburn. Both go up on hot days: temperature is a third variable driving the other two. Correlation shows that two things move together; it cannot say which, if either, causes the other. Deciding that needs an experiment or a reason from outside the data.

np.corrcoef returns NumPy numbers, so pearson converts the chosen entry with float before rounding it. The page's checker compares it with the same exact whole-number version used for the formula program.
zh: 给 np.corrcoef 两个列表，它返回的不是一个数。它把两个列表当成两个变量，返回一个 2 x 2 的矩阵：第 i 行第 j 列是变量 i 与变量 j 之间的 r。对角线是每个变量和它自己比，所以总是 1；两个非对角的格子是同一个 r，因为 x 对 y 的相关就是 y 对 x 的相关。所以 pearson 取第 0 行第 1 列——这是矩阵里唯一一个你事先不知道的数。
复习小时数对成绩，矩阵对角线是 1，另外两格是 0.964，与「照定义算皮尔逊相关系数」得到的 r 相同。把两个实参换个顺序，还是 0.964。
给 np.corrcoef 一个由几个列表组成的列表，每个列表都是一个变量：演示把温度、冰淇淋销量、晒伤人数一起传进去，得到 3 x 3 的矩阵。温度对冰淇淋 0.997，温度对晒伤 0.994，冰淇淋对晒伤 0.992。
最后这个数是强相关，可吃冰淇淋并不会让人晒伤。两者都在热天上升：温度是驱动它们俩的第三个变量。相关只说明两件事一起变化，说不出谁导致谁，甚至可能谁也不导致谁。要下这个结论，需要做实验，或者有数据之外的理由。
np.corrcoef 返回的是 NumPy 的数，所以 pearson 先用 float 转换取出的那一格，再舍入。页面的检查器拿照定义那个程序用的同一个整数精确版本和它对答案。

lineNotes.en: np.round rounds every entry of the array; NumPy prints 1 as '1.' to keep the columns lined up.
lineNotes.zh: np.round 把数组里每一格都舍入；NumPy 把 1 打印成「1.」，好让各列对齐。

lineNotes.en: 0.9 is only a rule of thumb for 'strong'; there is no official cut-off.
lineNotes.zh: 0.9 只是「强」的一个经验界线，没有官方标准。

[[1.    0.964]
 [0.964 1.   ]]
r: 0.964
swap the order: 0.964
temperature, ice creams, sunburns:
[[1.    0.997 0.994]

title.en: Line of Best Fit from the Formula
title.zh: 照公式求最佳拟合直线

blurb.en: The least-squares line y = a + bx worked out with NumPy arrays: gradient = sum of (x - x-bar)(y - y-bar) over sum of (x - x-bar) squared, intercept = y-bar - gradient times x-bar. Then predictions, and one that should not be trusted.
blurb.zh: 用 NumPy 数组算最小二乘直线 y = a + bx：斜率 = Σ(x - x̄)(y - ȳ) / Σ(x - x̄)²，截距 = ȳ - 斜率 × x̄。然后拿它预测，也看一个不该相信的预测。

en: The line of best fit (the least-squares regression line) is the straight line that makes the sum of the squared vertical distances from the points to the line as small as possible. Its gradient has a closed formula: the sum of the products of the deviations divided by the sum of the squared x deviations. The top of that fraction is the same sum that Pearson's r starts from.

Once the gradient is known, the intercept follows from one fact: the line always passes through the mean point (x-bar, y-bar). Put it into y = gradient times x + intercept and rearrange. For the eight students in the demo the mean point is (4.5, 65.5), and the line evaluated at 4.5 gives exactly 65.5.

For hours of revision against marks the gradient is 4.095 and the intercept 47.071: each extra hour is worth about 4.1 marks, and the line predicts about 47 marks for no revision at all. The predictions are 57.3 marks for 2.5 hours, 71.6 for 6 hours and 83.9 for 9 hours. A list made exactly from 3 times x minus 2 gives back (3.0, -2.0).

Predicting inside the range of the data (1 to 8 hours) is interpolation; outside it is extrapolation, and it can go badly wrong. The demo's last line asks about 40 hours and gets 210.9 marks - on a test out of 100. Nothing in the data says the straight line keeps going.

fit_line returns a tuple of two Python floats, each rounded to 9 places. Compare Line of Best Fit with np.polyfit, which gets the same pair from one library call. The page's checker compares both with a pure-Python version that works out the gradient and intercept exactly as fractions.
zh: 最佳拟合直线（最小二乘回归线）是让各点到直线的竖直距离平方和最小的那条直线。它的斜率有现成的公式：偏差乘积之和除以 x 偏差的平方和。分子正是皮尔逊 r 开头的那个和。
斜率知道了，截距由一个事实得出：这条直线一定经过均值点 (x̄, ȳ)。代进 y = 斜率 × x + 截距，移项即可。演示里八个学生的均值点是 (4.5, 65.5)，直线在 4.5 处的值正好是 65.5。
复习小时数对成绩，斜率 4.095、截距 47.071：每多复习一小时大约多 4.1 分，完全不复习时直线预测约 47 分。预测值：2.5 小时 57.3 分，6 小时 71.6 分，9 小时 83.9 分。用 3 乘 x 减 2 精确造出的列表，得回 (3.0, -2.0)。
在数据的范围之内（1 到 8 小时）预测叫内插；范围之外叫外推，可能错得离谱。演示最后一行问 40 小时，得到 210.9 分——满分 100 的考试。数据里没有任何东西说这条直线会一直延续下去。
fit_line 返回一个装着两个 Python 小数的元组，各舍入到 9 位。对照「用 np.polyfit 求最佳拟合直线」，它一次库函数调用就得到同一对数。页面的检查器拿一个纯 Python 版本和这两个都对答案：它用分数把斜率和截距算得分毫不差。

lineNotes.en: Two values separated by a comma make a tuple; float turns each NumPy number into a Python one first.
lineNotes.zh: 逗号隔开的两个值组成一个元组；float 先把每个 NumPy 数变成 Python 的数。

lineNotes.en: The format specifier :.3f shows three decimal places; the numbers themselves are not changed.
lineNotes.zh: 格式说明符 :.3f 显示三位小数；数本身没有被改动。

lineNotes.en: Extrapolation: 40 hours is far outside the data, and the answer is impossible.
lineNotes.zh: 外推：40 小时远在数据之外，答案不可能成立。

intercept: 47.071
line: mark = 4.095 * hours + 47.071

hours 6 -> predicted mark 71.6
hours 9 -> predicted mark 83.9
mean point: 4.5 65.5
line at the mean: 65.5

title.en: Line of Best Fit with np.polyfit
title.zh: 用 np.polyfit 求最佳拟合直线

blurb.en: The same line from one call: np.polyfit(x, y, 1) returns the gradient and then the intercept. Then the residuals - how far each point sits from the line - and why this line has the smallest sum of their squares.
blurb.zh: 同一条直线，一次调用：np.polyfit(x, y, 1) 先返回斜率、再返回截距。然后看残差——每个点离直线多远——以及为什么这条直线让残差平方和最小。

en: np.polyfit fits a polynomial of the degree you ask for; degree 1 is a straight line. It returns the coefficients as an array starting with the highest power, so for a line that is [gradient, intercept] - the demo prints 4.095 and 47.071, the same as Line of Best Fit from the Formula. Unpacking the array into two names on one line puts each in its own variable.

A residual is observed minus predicted: how far a point lies above (positive) or below (negative) the line. predicted and residuals are worked out for all eight points at once on the arrays. The residuals are 0.8, -0.3, 1.6, -5.5, 2.5, 2.4, -2.7 and 1.2 (to 1 place); the point furthest from the line is the student who revised for 4 hours, 5.5 marks below it.

Least squares means exactly this: of all straight lines, this one gives the smallest sum of squared residuals, 53.62 here. The demo tries a line with a gradient 0.5 steeper and the same intercept, and its sum is 104.62 - almost twice as big. Any other line you try would also come out bigger.
The residuals of a least-squares line always add up to zero (the positives and negatives balance), which is another way of saying the line passes through the mean point.

fit_line converts the two NumPy numbers with float and rounds each to 9 places. The page's checker compares it with a pure-Python version that works out the gradient and intercept exactly as fractions.
zh: np.polyfit 拟合你要求的次数的多项式；次数 1 就是直线。它返回的系数是一个数组，从最高次开始，所以对直线来说是 [斜率, 截距]——演示打印出 4.095 与 47.071，与「照公式求最佳拟合直线」相同。在一行里把数组解包给两个名字，两个数就各进各的变量。
残差是观测值减预测值：一个点在直线上方（正）或下方（负）多远。predicted 与 residuals 都在数组上对八个点一次算完。残差是 0.8、-0.3、1.6、-5.5、2.5、2.4、-2.7、1.2（保留 1 位）；离直线最远的是复习了 4 小时的那个学生，在直线下方 5.5 分。
最小二乘说的就是这件事：所有直线里，这一条的残差平方和最小，这里是 53.62。演示试了一条斜率大 0.5、截距相同的直线，它的平方和是 104.62——差不多翻倍。你试别的任何一条直线，结果也都会更大。
最小二乘直线的残差加起来总是零（正的和负的互相抵消），这等于换个说法讲「直线经过均值点」。
fit_line 用 float 转换两个 NumPy 数，各舍入到 9 位。页面的检查器拿一个纯 Python 版本和它对答案：它用分数把斜率和截距算得分毫不差。

lineNotes.en: argmax gives the index of the largest value; np.abs makes points below the line count as well.
lineNotes.zh: argmax 给出最大值的下标；np.abs 让直线下方的点也算进来。

lineNotes.en: Any change to the line makes the sum of squared residuals bigger.
lineNotes.zh: 对直线做任何改动，残差平方和都会变大。

blurb.en: Draw thousands of samples with rng.normal, take the mean of each, and watch the means cluster: their spread is sigma over the square root of n, so four times the sample size halves it.
blurb.zh: 用 rng.normal 抽几千组样本、每组求均值，看这些均值怎样聚拢：它们的散布是 σ 除以 √n，样本量翻四倍，散布减半。

en: One sample gives one mean, and a different sample would give a different one. The question here is how much sample means vary. The program draws 2000 samples of size n from a normal population with mean 50 and standard deviation 10, takes the mean of each, and looks at those 2000 means.

sample_means draws a whole table at once with rng.normal: repeats rows, n columns, one sample per row. Taking the mean along each row then gives one mean per sample. The generator rng is np.random.default_rng(2026), passed in as an argument; how default_rng works is on the Linear Algebra & Random Numbers page.

With this seed, the first sample of 4 is 42.1, 52.4, 31.0 and 64.0, and its mean is 47.37 - nearly 3 away from the true 50. The table then shows, for n = 4, 16 and 64, the mean of the 2000 means (49.99, 50.02, 50.02 - always close to 50) and their standard deviation (5.03, 2.36, 1.23) next to the theory, sigma over the square root of n (5.0, 2.5, 1.25). Each time n goes up four times, the spread halves.

This is the idea behind the central limit theorem: the sample mean is centred on the true mean, and its spread - the standard error - is sigma over the square root of n. With n = 16, 95.05% of the sample means were within 5 of 50 (two standard errors), and 69.2% within 2.5 (one standard error), close to the 95% and 68% of a normal distribution. Single values, by contrast, were within 5 of 50 only 38.5% of the time.
The page does not draw a histogram; the numbers carry the shape. Another seed gives slightly different numbers and the same pattern.
zh: 一组样本给出一个均值，换一组样本就会得到另一个。这里的问题是：样本均值会变动多少。程序从均值 50、标准差 10 的正态总体里抽 2000 组、每组 n 个，每组求均值，再看这 2000 个均值。
sample_means 用 rng.normal 一次抽出一整张表：repeats 行、n 列，每行一组样本。再对每一行求均值，每组样本得到一个均值。生成器 rng 是 np.random.default_rng(2026)，当实参传进去；default_rng 怎么用见「线性代数与随机数」一页。
这就是中心极限定理背后的直觉：样本均值以真正的均值为中心，它的散布——标准误——是 σ / √n。n = 16 时，95.05% 的样本均值落在 50 的 5 以内（两个标准误），69.2% 落在 2.5 以内（一个标准误），接近正态分布的 95% 与 68%。相比之下，单个的值只有 38.5% 落在 50 的 5 以内。
这一页不画直方图；分布的形状由数字说出来。换一个种子，数字会略有不同，规律不变。

lineNotes.en: One generator with a fixed seed: the same numbers on every run.
lineNotes.zh: 一个种子固定的生成器：每次运行都是同一串数。

lineNotes.en: The mean of a boolean array is the share of True values.
lineNotes.zh: 布尔数组的均值就是 True 所占的比例。

title.zh: 用 NormalDist 求正态概率

blurb.en: statistics.NormalDist does the normal-distribution tables for you: cdf for 'at most', differences of cdf for 'between', inv_cdf to go backwards from a probability to a value. Then 68-95-99.7, and a simulation that agrees.
blurb.zh: statistics.NormalDist 替你查正态分布表：cdf 求「不超过」，cdf 相减求「之间」，inv_cdf 从概率倒推回数值。然后是 68-95-99.7 规则，以及一个与之吻合的模拟。

en: NormalDist(170, 8) is a normal distribution with mean 170 and standard deviation 8 - say, heights in centimetres. Its cdf(x) is the probability of a value at most x: the area under the bell curve to the left of x. For heights under 180 that is 0.8944. 'More than' is 1 minus cdf: heights over 185 have probability 0.0304.

'Between a and b' is cdf(b) - cdf(a): the area to the left of b with the area to the left of a taken away. prob_between does exactly that; between 160 and 180 the answer is 0.7887. A single exact value has probability 0 - the width of the interval is zero - which is why a question about a continuous measurement always asks about a range.

inv_cdf goes the other way: give it a probability and it gives the value with that much of the distribution below it. The tallest 5% are over 183.2 cm, and the middle half of people lie between 164.6 and 175.4 cm (the 25% and 75% points).

The loop checks the 68-95-99.7 rule on the standard normal distribution (mean 0, standard deviation 1): within 1 standard deviation of the mean lies 0.6827 of the probability, within 2 lies 0.9545, within 3 lies 0.9973.

The last part simulates the same heights: 100000 draws from rng.normal(170, 8), with the generator np.random.default_rng(7). With this seed, 0.79 of the draws fall between 160 and 180 and 0.0299 are over 185, close to the exact 0.7887 and 0.0304; another seed gives slightly different shares. The boolean arrays are combined with &, and the mean of a boolean array is the share of True values.
prob_between itself only uses the standard library. The page's checker compares it with a pure-Python numerical integration of the bell curve (Simpson's rule), a different route to the same area.
zh: NormalDist(170, 8) 是一个均值 170、标准差 8 的正态分布——比如以厘米计的身高。它的 cdf(x) 是取值不超过 x 的概率：钟形曲线下、x 左边的面积。身高不到 180 的概率是 0.8944。「超过」就是 1 减 cdf：身高超过 185 的概率是 0.0304。
「在 a 与 b 之间」是 cdf(b) - cdf(a)：b 左边的面积去掉 a 左边的面积。prob_between 做的正是这件事；160 与 180 之间的答案是 0.7887。恰好等于某一个值的概率是 0——区间的宽度为零——所以关于连续测量的问题总是问一个范围。
inv_cdf 反过来走：给它一个概率，它给出「有这么多比例在它以下」的那个值。最高的 5% 在 183.2 厘米以上，中间一半的人在 164.6 与 175.4 厘米之间（25% 与 75% 两个分位点）。
循环在标准正态分布（均值 0、标准差 1）上核对 68-95-99.7 规则：离均值 1 个标准差以内占 0.6827，2 个以内占 0.9545，3 个以内占 0.9973。
最后一部分模拟同样的身高：用 rng.normal(170, 8) 抽 100000 个，生成器是 np.random.default_rng(7)。这个种子下，0.79 的抽样落在 160 与 180 之间，0.0299 超过 185，与精确值 0.7887、0.0304 很接近；换一个种子，比例会略有不同。布尔数组用 & 组合，布尔数组的均值就是 True 所占的比例。
prob_between 本身只用标准库。页面的检查器拿一个纯 Python 的数值积分（辛普森法）和它对答案：对钟形曲线求面积，走的是另一条路。

lineNotes.en: A distribution object: the mean first, then the standard deviation.
lineNotes.zh: 一个分布对象：先均值，后标准差。

lineNotes.en: & combines two boolean arrays item by item; each comparison needs its own brackets.
lineNotes.zh: & 把两个布尔数组逐项组合；每个比较都要自己的一对括号。

blurb.en: A first hypothesis test: H0 says the mean is what was claimed, H1 says it is not. Work out z from the sample mean, turn it into a two-sided p-value with NormalDist, compare with 5%, and word the conclusion carefully.
blurb.zh: 第一个假设检验：H0 说均值就是声称的那个值，H1 说不是。由样本均值算出 z，用 NormalDist 把它变成双侧 p 值，与 5% 比较，再小心地措辞结论。

en: A factory says its machine fills bags with 500 g of flour on average, and the spread is known: sigma = 4 g. Ten bags are weighed. The null hypothesis H0 is that the true mean is 500; the alternative H1 is that it is not 500 (either way, so the test is two-sided).

If H0 is true, the mean of n bags has standard deviation sigma over the square root of n - the standard error. z is how many standard errors the sample mean lies from 500. The p-value is the probability, if H0 were true, of a z at least that far from 0 in either direction: twice the area in one tail of the standard normal curve, which NormalDist() (mean 0, standard deviation 1) gives through its cdf.

For the bags the mean is 497.4, z is -2.055 and p is 0.0398. That is below the significance level of 5%, so H0 is rejected: there is evidence at the 5% level that the mean fill is not 500 g. For the light bulbs (claimed 1000 hours, sigma 15) the mean is 1001.75, z is 0.33 and p is 0.7414, far above 5%, so H0 is not rejected.

The wording matters. Not rejecting H0 is not the same as proving it: the bulbs' data are simply consistent with 1000 hours. And rejecting H0 at the 5% level means that data this extreme would turn up less than 5% of the time if H0 were true - not that H0 has a 5% chance of being true.
The last line gives the critical value 1.96: a two-sided test at 5% rejects exactly when |z| is more than 1.96, which is the same decision as p < 0.05.

z_test returns z and p rounded to 6 places and the decision as a bool, worked out from the unrounded p. The page's checker compares it with a version that finds the tail area by numerical integration of the bell curve (Simpson's rule) instead of NormalDist; its test samples are centred on the claimed mean, a little off it, and far off it, so that both decisions come up.
zh: 工厂说它的机器平均每袋装 500 克面粉，而且离散程度已知：σ = 4 克。称了十袋。原假设 H0：真正的均值是 500；备择假设 H1：不是 500（偏哪边都算，所以是双侧检验）。
如果 H0 成立，n 袋的均值的标准差是 σ 除以 √n——标准误。z 是样本均值离 500 有几个标准误。p 值是：假如 H0 成立，得到一个离 0 至少这么远（向哪边都算）的 z 的概率——标准正态曲线一侧尾巴面积的两倍，由 NormalDist()（均值 0、标准差 1）的 cdf 给出。
面粉袋的均值是 497.4，z 是 -2.055，p 是 0.0398。它低于 5% 的显著性水平，所以拒绝 H0：在 5% 水平上有证据表明平均装量不是 500 克。灯泡（声称 1000 小时，σ = 15）的均值是 1001.75，z 是 0.33，p 是 0.7414，远高于 5%，所以不拒绝 H0。
措辞很要紧。不拒绝 H0 不等于证明了它：灯泡的数据只是与 1000 小时相符。而在 5% 水平上拒绝 H0 的意思是：假如 H0 成立，这么极端的数据出现的机会不到 5%——不是说 H0 为真的概率是 5%。
最后一行给出临界值 1.96：5% 的双侧检验恰好在 |z| 大于 1.96 时拒绝，与 p < 0.05 是同一个判决。
z_test 返回舍入到 6 位的 z 与 p，以及用未舍入的 p 得出的判决（布尔值）。页面的检查器拿另一个版本和它对答案：它不用 NormalDist，而是对钟形曲线做数值积分（辛普森法）求尾巴面积；它造的测试样本有的以声称的均值为中心、有的偏一点、有的偏很多，两种判决都会出现。

lineNotes.en: Plain Python: the sample mean, with no NumPy needed.
lineNotes.zh: 纯 Python：样本均值，用不着 NumPy。

lineNotes.en: 2.5% in each tail leaves 97.5% below the upper critical value.
lineNotes.zh: 两边尾巴各 2.5%，上临界值以下就是 97.5%。

title.zh: 单样本 t 统计量

blurb.en: When the population's standard deviation is unknown, estimate it from the sample and the z statistic becomes t = (x-bar - mu0) / (s / sqrt(n)). Compare it with a critical value from a t table for n - 1 degrees of freedom.
blurb.zh: 总体的标准差未知时，用样本去估计它，z 统计量就变成 t = (x̄ - μ0) / (s / √n)。再拿它与 t 分布表里自由度 n - 1 的临界值比较。

en: The z-test needs the population's standard deviation sigma, and in real life it is usually unknown. The t statistic replaces sigma with s, the sample standard deviation - the ddof=1 version from Population and Sample Standard Deviation - and otherwise has the same shape as z.

Because s is itself only an estimate, t varies more than z would, especially for small samples. So t is compared with a larger critical value, taken from the t distribution with n - 1 degrees of freedom. Working out a p-value for t needs that distribution, which the standard library does not have (it is in the scipy library, not used on this page), so here the critical value is looked up in a table, the way an exam question gives it: 2.262 for 9 degrees of freedom and 2.776 for 4, both two-sided at 5%.

Battery life, claimed 20 hours: the ten batteries give t = -4.576 with 9 degrees of freedom. |t| is bigger than 2.262, so H0 (a mean of 20 hours) is rejected at the 5% level - the batteries seem to last less.

Long jump, claimed 4.8 m: five jumps give t = 1.812 with 4 degrees of freedom. |t| is smaller than 2.776, so H0 is not rejected. The last line makes the point about small samples: with a known sigma the cut-off would be 1.96, but with only 5 values and an estimated spread the cut-off is 2.776.
The wording of the conclusions follows the same rules as in One-Sample z-Test: not rejecting H0 does not prove it.
zh: z 检验需要总体的标准差 σ，而现实里它通常不知道。t 统计量用样本标准差 s 顶替 σ——就是「总体标准差与样本标准差」里 ddof=1 的那个——其余与 z 同一个形状。
因为 s 本身只是个估计，t 比 z 变动得更厉害，样本小的时候尤其如此。所以 t 要跟一个更大的临界值比，这个值取自自由度为 n - 1 的 t 分布。要给 t 算 p 值就得用到这个分布，而标准库里没有（它在 scipy 库里，这一页不用），所以这里照考题的给法查表：自由度 9 是 2.262，自由度 4 是 2.776，都是双侧 5%。
电池续航，声称 20 小时：十节电池给出 t = -4.576，自由度 9。|t| 大于 2.262，所以在 5% 水平上拒绝 H0（均值 20 小时）——这些电池似乎撑不了那么久。
跳远，声称 4.8 米：五次跳跃给出 t = 1.812，自由度 4。|t| 小于 2.776，所以不拒绝 H0。最后一行点出小样本的要害：σ 已知时临界值只要 1.96，可只有 5 个值、离散程度又是估计出来的，临界值就是 2.776。
结论的措辞与「单样本 z 检验」同样的规矩：不拒绝 H0 不等于证明了它。

lineNotes.en: A small t table keyed by degrees of freedom: two-sided, 5% significance level.
lineNotes.zh: 一张按自由度查的小 t 表：双侧，5% 显著性水平。

lineNotes.en: A one-sample t-test has n - 1 degrees of freedom.
lineNotes.zh: 一样本 t 检验的自由度是 n - 1。
